# Review — iliad-085 (Iliad 13.748–837), reviewer pass 1 (two internal passes)

Edited `units.json` in place by script; `t` verified unchanged unit by unit against the pre-review copy. All notes are still ≤110 words (longest 108). `new-renderings.md` synced to every rendering changed. No build run. No gloss.json was in the folder, so no parse in it was checked. No line was flagged for scansion, so none was hand-scanned and no scansion sentence was added.

Totals: 17 rows (19 field edits) — high 0, medium 4 rows (5 field edits: 775 l, 775 n, 795 n, 837 l/i, 837 n), low 13 rows. No finding left open as an error; open uncertainties at the end.

## Findings considered and refused

- **οἴω 781 (dual of οἶος vs ὀΐω ‘I think’).** Kept as dual. Reasons: οἴχεσθον is a finite dual verb, so ὀΐω would have nothing to govern (it needs accusative and infinitive); τετυμμένω and ἀμφοτέρω are duals; the sense “only the two have gone, both wounded” follows 780 (the others were killed). The same dual οἴω is already published at Odyssey 11.512 (odyssey-055: “Nestor … and I, we two alone”, `l` “we two alone”, `i` “Only godlike Nestor and I”), where the note says “οἴω is the dual”. The published Iliad uses of οἴω (iliad-029, -055, -059, -070) are all ὀΐω ‘I think’ with an infinitive, which is why this one needs its note. `l` “The two alone”, `i` “Only” agree with the Odyssey wording.
- **υἷ’ Ἱπποτίωνος 792 (dual or singular).** Dual kept (υἷ’ = υἷε, ‘Ascanius and Morys’), with the note stating the singular possibility; only the `i` was changed (item 6). The singular υἷα would leave Ascanius without a father in the line and is not the usual reading.
- **ἐρωῆσαι 776.** Rendering “hold back from war” kept (ἐρωέω “draw back, retire” is intransitive); note repaired (item 3). Meaning of ἄλλοτε … μᾶλλον … μέλλω (‘at some other time I am likelier to hold back more’) kept as drafted.
- **ἀμοιβοί 793.** “as replacements” kept: ἀμοιβός ‘in exchange, relieving’ is the sense Cunliffe and LSJ give for troops coming to relieve others; note says so.
- **ταλάσσῃς 829.** Aorist subjunctive of ταλάσσω (root of τλῆναι) after αἴ κε, with μεῖναι; “bring yourself to await” matches the table’s τλάω aorist “bring oneself” (11.350). Label in note is true.
- **Τρώων κύνας 831.** Genitive goes with κύνας ἠδ’ οἰωνούς (‘the Trojans’ dogs and birds’), not partitive as with τις at 8.379 (iliad-049 checked: τις καὶ Τρώων). The note’s contrast is true; `l` “the dogs and birds of the Trojans” and `i` “the Trojans’ dogs and birds” agree. Second line identical to the published `l` (and `i` differs only in person, “your”).
- **ἐν τείχει 764.** “within the wall” kept; note says the wall is not named and is probably Troy’s.
- **751 imperative.** “you hold all the best men back here” can be read as indicative in isolation. Refused: σὺ μέν … αὐτὰρ ἐγώ needs “you” against “I”, 752 is fixed by the published line, and the note names ἐρύκακε as an imperative. Alternative wordings add “must” or “stay” that the Greek lacks.
- **“which your lily-like skin will tear” (829–831 `l`).** The Greek word order itself is ambiguous between subject and object; `l` follows it and `i` clarifies. Kept.
- **ἐπελήλατο `i` “hammered”.** Looks like a departure from “drive”, but 7.223 (ἤλασε χαλκόν, `l` “drove … bronze”, `i` “hammered on … a layer, of bronze”) is the precedent; recorded in new-renderings.md.
- **750 μιν “to him” / “to Polydamas”.** Departure from 1.201 is justified (μιν is Polydamas) and has the precedent of 2.7 (“to it” / “the Dream”).
- **Marks.** Hector speaks (751, 769), Alexander answers (775, after the reply formula 774), Ajax speaks (810), Hector answers (824, after ἀμείβετο) agree with the published usage (iliad-081, -082, -084). “Ajax speaks” kept (only one Ajax in this part; the Telamonian is identified in the note).
- **Title.** ἀπειλαί means ‘threats’, English says ‘Taunts’. Left alone: title and `part` must match the manifest/parts, and both threats and taunts occur in the part. Noted as open.
- **Πάλμύν 792.** Two accents (ά, ύ) as in the archive; `t` is not to be touched.
- **τί ἢ 810** — the grave on ἢ is printed by the edition; I did not change the reading, only the note’s claim (item 11).
- **Δηΐφοβον in the note on 758.** Written with the lemma accent (ΐ), not the enclitic-shifted accent of t (Δηΐφοβόν τε); correct as a quoted form.

Line-level repeats (748–749 iliad-072/-016; 752 iliad-075; 769 iliad-016; 785–786 odyssey-112; 788 iliad-042; 816 iliad-011; 821 odyssey-072; 827–828 iliad-051; 831b–832 iliad-049; 833 iliad-074; 780 νωλεμέως iliad-077; 803 first line iliad-078) reuse the published English.

## Open uncertainties

1. αὐγάς 837: changed to “rays” by my own reading of the table (glare for fire/bronze/lightning, rays for sun); the owner may prefer to keep “glare” as at 2.456 and 13.244.
2. 13.775–777: the exact force of ἄλλοτε δή ποτε μᾶλλον … ἐρωῆσαι μέλλω is disputed; `l`/`i` follow one reading, as drafted.
3. 13.792: dual vs singular υἷ’ is a real textual-grammatical doubt; the English commits to ‘the two sons’.
4. Title ἀπειλαί / “Taunts”.

## Pass 2 (reviewer pass 2; gloss.json read for the first time)

All 17 `__broaden__` entries were checked to be the old known-forms entry whole + ` · ` + a true new reading. No ASCII apostrophe, backtick, line number or "here" in any entry; new entries all under 230 characters. `t` verified unchanged unit by unit; notes still at most 108 words. No build run.
